questions.q: What do versionAsOf and timestampAsOf let you do?
options: Create a brand-new table from scratch with historical data
Delete all versions except the one specified
Permanently roll the table back to an earlier state
Query a Delta table exactly as it looked at a past version or a past point in time
questions.explain: Both return an ordinary DataFrame — every Foundations Chapter 4 method still works on it.

questions.q: Why is time travel possible at all?
options: Time travel actually re-runs every transformation from scratch each time
Delta keeps a separate full backup copy of the table for every single write
A "remove" action (Lesson 17) marks a file as no longer current but usually doesn't delete it from disk immediately, so old versions can still be reconstructed
It relies on a totally separate database unrelated to the Delta log
questions.explain: The log records exactly which files a past version depended on, and those files are often still present.

questions.q: What does RESTORE TABLE trips TO VERSION AS OF 3 do, compared to just querying that version?
options: It's a deliberate action that makes version 3 become the current version again, unlike a query which leaves the table unchanged
It deletes every version after version 3 immediately
It has the exact same effect as querying — nothing actually changes
It only works if Unity Catalog is enabled
questions.explain: This is useful for undoing a bad write, like a botched MERGE, cleanly.

questions.q: Why is time travel not a substitute for a real backup strategy?
options: Time travel can only be used once per table, ever
Time travel only works for tables smaller than 1GB
VACUUM (Lesson 24) deletes files no longer referenced by the current version past a retention window, after which those old versions become unqueryable
Time travel data is stored in a completely separate, unreliable location
questions.explain: The default retention window is 30 days — a useful safety net for recent history, not permanent backup.

questions.q: Does querying an old version with versionAsOf change the current state of the table?
options: No — only RESTORE TABLE actually changes which version is current
It depends on whether the read used SQL or the DataFrame API
Yes, querying an old version automatically makes it the new current version
Yes, but only if the query includes a WHERE clause
questions.explain: Querying is read-only; RESTORE is the deliberate, table-changing action.
